summary: All ten TDD-anchor scenarios are covered with meaningful, litmus-positive assertions. The three new/rewritten test files use only servlet-stack APIs (no StepVerifier / WebTestClient / MockServerWebExchange / reactor-test) and the deleted RememberMeWebSessionIdResolverTest is gone from the tree. Two minor structural issues worth noting: GlobalErrorHandlerTest splits the anchor 'handleAppException_handleResponseStatus_handleThrowable_unchanged' into five granular methods (broader than the anchor — not a regression), and SecurityConfigTest has one redundant duplicate assertion plus one weak negative assertion (isNotEqualTo(403)) on the webhook path.

findings.issue: Webhook-bypass assertion uses 'status != 403', which is defensive but weak: a 500 from a misconfigured controller would silently pass the CSRF-bypass check even if the AND-scoped matcher had regressed in a way that mapped to a different error code. The intent (no CSRF challenge) is captured indirectly.
findings.suggestion: Sharpen by also reading the response body / header for a CSRF-rejection marker, OR pin the expected reach-through status (most likely 401 since the webhook gate is unauthenticated at this stack level — controller secret-header gate runs later). If the controller may not be wired at Wave 2 commit boundary, add a comment justifying the loose check and keep status=403 specifically as the regression marker, e.g. `.andExpect(status().value(not(403)))` with a clarifying message.

findings.issue: Performs the same GET /health twice (lines 76-83 then 86-87) to assert cookie presence via two styles. The second perform/expect adds zero coverage — same path, same verb, same matcher semantics — but doubles execution cost on a SpringBootTest context.
findings.suggestion: Drop the second `mockMvc.perform(get("/health")).andExpect(cookie().exists("XSRF-TOKEN"))` block — the manual `Cookie xsrf = ...` assertion + value-not-blank check already pins the regression. If you want the higher-level matcher style instead, replace the manual block; do not duplicate.

findings.issue: The TDD anchor specifies one named test 'handleAppException_handleResponseStatus_handleThrowable_unchanged' but the file splits it into seven granular methods (appException_400/401/403/409/429, handleResponseStatus_propagatesStatusAndReason, throwable_returns500_withoutExposingDetails). Coverage is broader and stronger, but the literal name from the anchor is missing — downstream automation that greps for the anchor name will report it as absent.
findings.suggestion: No behavioral fix needed. If the team automates anchor presence via grep on method names, either (a) keep the granular methods and add a one-line comment header listing them as fulfilling the umbrella anchor, or (b) add a single facade test method `handleAppException_handleResponseStatus_handleThrowable_unchanged` that invokes the three handlers with one assertion each and let the granular ones provide depth. Behavioural coverage already exceeds the anchor.
